Vpi 1.7 V from Fig. 3(c) (100 kHz triangular drive; wavelength not stated, the paper says C-band); VpiL 2.13 V cm is the authors' 1.7 V x 12.5 mm; the simulated VpiL 2.4 V cm (58.2 percent LN confinement, push-pull) is not entered. drive push_pull and vpi_convention mzm_push_pull follow the supplement p.3 statement that the VpiL derivation assumes the push-pull configuration of the device; the measurement text does not name it. Bandwidth: bw3db_ghz 67 with gt is the end of the measured EO S21 trace (Fig. 4(e), p.4): the trace stays above about -2.4 dB up to its end near 67 GHz (about -2.3 dB there), so only 'more than 67 GHz' is shown by the data; bw_measured_to_ghz 67 (both extracted_from_figure). The paper claims '>70 GHz' (abstract, p.2, p.4, Table 1, conclusions) beyond the plotted measurement; that claim is not entered as a value. The EE S21 (6.4 dB point) 'surpasses 67 GHz' (Fig. 4(a)); the trace also ends at 67 GHz. The simulated 3 dB point of 100 GHz (p.4, model with the measured electrode parameters, green curve in Fig. 4(e)) is not entered. EO response normalisation frequency not stated. Loss: 2 dB insertion loss and 25 dB ER were measured before electrode deposition with the grating couplers normalised out (Fig. 3(b)); after full fabrication the chip loss is 10.2 dB including 7.2 dB for the two grating couplers, giving the 3 dB on-chip loss stated in the conclusion and Table 1 (10.2 - 7.2); the authors attribute the extra 1 dB to the metal electrodes. Hybrid-waveguide propagation loss is an author estimate (1.6 dB/cm, before electrodes). RF: fitted alpha0 0.49 dB/cm/GHz^0.5 (Fig. 4(d)) gives 4.01 dB/cm at 67 GHz (derived); n_rf about 2.6 is the plateau of Fig. 4(c) (design 2.5); the deduced Z0 ripples between about 48 and 55 ohm (Fig. 4(b)) so z0_ohm is empty; simulated Z0 50 ohm, n_rf 2.5 and alpha0 0.21 are not entered; ng 2.5 is the simulated optical group index marked in Fig. 2(d) and Fig. 4(c). CLTW dimensions (r,c,s,t,h,w,L) = (47,3,3,5,19,13,36) um (p.3), period r + c = 50 um (supplement p.3); T-structure thickness 200 nm. Data: dynamic ER better than 8 dB and drive voltages less than 2 V for all eyes (amplitude type not stated); eyes up to 168 Gbit/s; max_baud_gbd 100 is the 100 Gbit/s OOK line rate (derived). Not reported: measurement wavelength, optical input power, sidewall angle, Si substrate thickness, energy per bit, measured Z0.

Resonance near 1568 nm read from Fig. 3(e),(f) (L band; the design resonance is near 1559 nm, Fig. 1(i), shifted by process variation, p.4). Tuning efficiency 24.33 pm/V (Fig. 3(g), Fig. S2(b)); on the reversed voltage axis of Fig. 3(g) (+30 V to -30 V) the resonance blue-shifts for positive voltage (-0.8 nm at +30 V, +0.7 nm at -30 V; Fig. 3(f): the +30 V peak lies at shorter wavelength), so the signed value is -24.33 pm/V (the text and the figure label quote the magnitude; signed-value convention as for the other Pockels resonators in the database). Q 2200 (p.2, 'a Q factor of 2200', type and unit-cell number not stated at that sentence; Fig. 3(d) gives Q 1118 to 3848 for N = 50 to 90). Bandwidth: the small-signal EO S21 (Fig. 3(h)) was measured with a 110 GHz lightwave component analyzer at detunings 0.85 to 1.25 nm; it peaks at about +7 to +9 dB near 60-100 GHz and stays above the -3 dB line to 110 GHz, so >110 GHz with the measurement limit 110 GHz; the gap of the device used for Fig. 3(h) is not stated (assigned here by judgment, as the headline device). Drive 3 Vpp is the amplifier output stated in the Experimental Section; cable and probe loss not stated. max_baud 220 GBd is the 220 Gb/s NRZ eye (derived); BER measured only to 100 Gb/s NRZ (limited AWG). Not reported: ER, Vpi, optical input power, temperature.
